# Policy Test Suite

The policy test suite generates a policy for a Kubernetes resource and evaluates recorded Kata agent RPCs against it.
Run it from the repository root with `just policy`.

## Directory layout

Each subdirectory of this directory is one test resource:

```
<name>/
├── resource.yml   # Kubernetes resource the policy is generated for
├── base.json      # Recorded agent RPCs, all expected to be allowed
└── *.json         # Test cases, as JSON patches on base.json
```

`resource.yml` must contain exactly one pod-generating resource with `runtimeClassName: contrast-cc` and the pod label `app.kubernetes.io/name: test-<name>`.
Only images defined in `packages/by-name/policy-test/package.nix` can be used, referenced exactly by the `ref` given there.

`base.json` is a list of `{"kind": ..., "allowed": ..., "request": ...}` entries, evaluated in order against the policy rule `<kind>`.
It's generated by `just policy-rpc` on a running cluster, don't edit it by hand.

## Writing a test case

Add a `<name>.json` file containing an [RFC 6902 JSON patch](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6902) that modifies a request in `base.json` and sets the expected result.

```json
[
  { "op": "test", "path": "/1/kind", "value": "CreateSandboxRequest" },
  { "op": "replace", "path": "/1/request/sandbox_pidns", "value": true },
  { "op": "replace", "path": "/1/allowed", "value": false }
]
```

To test a new resource, add a directory with a `resource.yml` and run `just policy-rpc` to record its `base.json`.
This deploys every resource, records its agent RPCs with `get-agent-rpcs.sh`, and replaces dynamic values like IDs and IP addresses with placeholders using `normalize-agent-rpcs.jq`.

The label `app.kubernetes.io/name` must be set to `test-<name>` for the `get-agent-rpcs.sh` script to find the pod and record its RPCs.
Resource names must be unique per kind and should match the app label.
Pod controllers like Deployments and DaemonSets append random suffixes from the alphabet `bcdfghjklmnpqrstvwxz2456789` to pod names.
The normalization can't distinguish these from a name segment consisting only of these characters, so the last dash-separated segment of `<name>` must contain at least one other character (for example, `test-ds` and `test-my-ds` break, `test-daemonset` works).
